title: Can we trust AI outputs? Learning what deterministic verifiers can, and cannot, guarantee
description:
Teaching materials for the NeurIPS 2026 Education Track. The lesson comes in two formats: a self-contained Jupyter notebook (ipywidgets) and a single HTML page that runs Python in the browser through Pyodide. Learners build a deterministic verifier for de-identifying four synthetic patient records, close a generate-verify-feedback-retry loop, and meet the verifier's limits: loud and quiet failures, string gaps and world gaps, and how an imperfect verifier becomes a training reward (RLVR, reward hacking). A facilitator guide is included.

Code is released under MIT (LICENSE-CODE). Prose, figures, synthetic records and recorded model attempts are CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-CONTENT). All records are invented; no real person is represented.
